questions.q: What rule did Amundsen's team follow to reach the South Pole?
a: Walk 20 miles every day, whatever the weather
Travel as far as possible on good days
Rest whenever conditions turned bad
Follow a route mapped by earlier explorers
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the 20 Mile March: a fixed daily distance regardless of conditions.

questions.q: Why did the daily 20-mile rule work so well?
a: It conserved energy and produced steady progress
It let the team arrive weeks ahead of schedule
It required fewer supplies than planned
It kept the men warm during storms
questions.why: Lesson 1 says holding back on good days and pushing on bad ones conserved resources.

Attack competitors before they can respond
Hire fast, then cut staff once demand is clear

questions.why: Lesson 2 says Apple tested the iPod and iTunes on a small scale before going wide.

questions.q: How did Apple apply this to the iPod?
a: It first tested a Mac-only iPod and iTunes, then expanded
It released the iPod and iTunes worldwide on day one
It bought an existing music company outright
It licensed the design to other electronics firms
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the Mac-only iPod and iTunes as low-risk tests before the wider release.
